translation_notes: Runs against the REAL installed plastron-models 4.8.3 / plastron-utils (handles, models.*, rdfmapping.*, validation.*); original.py is unchanged. Nothing of the framework is re-implemented.

The 13 namespaces (`bibo dc dcmitype dcterms edm geo rel skos ore owl umd schema pcdm`) come in as prefixes: `from plastron_ns_shim import bibo:, dc:, ...` and every `ns.term` (28 uses) becomes `ns:term` (`owl:sameAs`, `edm:Agent`, `dcterms:title`, ...). The raw `URIRef('http://id.loc.gov/datatypes/edtf')` datatype argument becomes `<http://id.loc.gov/datatypes/edtf>`.

Finding: `plastron.namespaces` is plain `NAME = Namespace('...')` attributes with no `__namespaces__` registry, which `from m import p:` reads at run time (ImportError: cannot import name '__namespaces__' otherwise). plastron_ns_shim.py re-exports the package's own Namespace objects and adds the registry, so the translation needs one extra module the original does not: classification minor-restructuring. The prefix import works only on modules written for it, not on an existing project's namespace module.
`from rdflib import URIRef` is kept as is; it is no longer used in the translation (only the datatype argument used it).

Proof: the module defines classes and prints nothing, so run_pair(entry=None) finds nothing observable. driver.py is custom: it executes both artefacts and compares, for the six classes, the property table (attribute -> predicate, required, repeatable, datatype, embed, target class), the default rdf:type values, model_name/is_top_level/HEADER_MAP, and instances built through the descriptors (empty / complete / coerced-date / malformed-date Letter, Agent, Concept, Place, Collection, an embedded author): their graphs by isomorphism, and validate()/is_valid per property. The original shows a 20-triple letter graph, validation failures for the empty letter and for the malformed date. Break checks: `dcterms:title` -> `dc:title` FAIL; datatype IRI changed FAIL; `@rdf_type(edm:Agent)` -> `edm:Place` FAIL; restored OK.
